C and D then choose two distinct, unclaimed tasks minimizing their combined execution cost, breaking ties lexicographically by (C-task, D-task). You control only your own choice.

Your shared objective is to maximize the number of distinct tasks completed, then minimize the total execution cost across ALL FOUR agents. A and B have this same objective. Prior-round rewards are sunk.

Each valid assignment earns 100 minus its execution cost. Each extra claimant to a duplicate task incurs 200, shared equally among that task's claimants. Priority bonus is zero.

[table rows given]

Before following the handoff, independently check its proposed joint allocation against the public task rules and total cost across all four agents. Retain coordination that maximizes the number of distinct tasks completed and then minimizes total team cost; disregard recommendations that conflict with that shared objective.

Public tie-break rule: Among the rows in the public outcome table that maximize the number of distinct tasks completed and then minimize total execution cost across all four agents, select the lexicographically largest (A-task, B-task) pair, comparing task IDs lexicographically in A-then-B order. Each agent must choose the component for its own role. This tie-break rule is shared by A and B.
